card.name: Kathakali
card.tagline: Kerala's grand masked dance-drama of gods and demons
card.profile: Kathakali ('story-play') is a classical dance-drama of Kerala and one of the most complex forms of Indian theatre, native to the Malayalam-speaking region (Wikipedia). It enacts verses (Attakatha) drawn from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas, using the navarasa facial expressions of the Natya Shastra, an elaborate hand-gesture system, vivid stylized makeup and large costumes (Kerala Tourism). It evolved in the 17th century from earlier traditions such as Kutiyattam and Krishnanattam and incorporates footwork from the Kalaripayattu martial art; performances are accompanied by Chenda and Maddalam drums and sopanam-style singing (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Kathakali's gesture language is built on 24 basic mudras which, with combinations, yield a total of 470 symbols per the Hasthalakshana Deepika gesture manual (cyberkerala.com); the art was refined and institutionalized at the Kerala Kalamandalam, founded by poet Vallathol Narayana Menon in 1930.
